articles.title: How Vin Bui became engineer #1 at Nowadays — and started treating it like his own company
articles.summary: Vin found Nowadays on Work at a Startup, saw a codebase he could fix, and joined as the first engineer. Now he builds AI voice tools and mentors the team.

articles.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Feedback on Handwritten Mathematics: Feedback Quality and Subsequent Exam Performance
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate the quality of feedback and practice exercises generated by GPT-5.1 from handwritten university mathematics answers and their grades, and examine whether receiving this feedback improves subsequent exam performance. We use six weekly bonus tests in an English (n=343) and a Dutch (n=236) cohort. Tests 1 and 3 used a crossover feedback design; otherwise, all attendees received feedback. articles.title: Large Language Models for Agent-Based Modelling: Current and possible uses across the modelling cycle
articles.summary: arXiv:2507.05723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) with increasingly sophisticated natural language understanding and generative capabilities has sparked interest in the Agent-based Modelling (ABM) community. With their ability to summarize, generate, analyze, categorize, transcribe and translate text, answer questions, propose explanations, sustain dialogue, extract information from unstructured text, and perform logical reasoning and problem-solving tasks, LLMs have a good potential to contribute to the modelling process. articles.title: An AI Security Agent for University ACMIS: Multi-Vector Threat Detection and Automated Response
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.08270v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: University Academic Management Information Systems (ACMIS) are high-value targets for a wide spectrum of security threats including brute-force login attacks, payment fraud, privilege escalation, insider data theft, and academic integrity violations. Traditional rule-based intrusion detection systems are inadequate because many malicious activities are structurally indistinguishable from normal operations. articles.title: Atlas of MICCAI: 28 Years of Representation, Collaboration, and the Road to Inclusion
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific knowledge in medical image analysis is shaped by venues such as the Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention (MICCAI) conference, which influence research agendas, professional credibility, and access to opportunity. As AI methods increasingly depend on large-scale data and compute, these dynamics risk further concentrating influence within already well-resourced regions and institutions. articles.title: Evidence-Grounded LLM-Assisted Android Mobile Forensic Reporting
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.26946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can assist forensic report drafting, but fluent output does not ensure evidentiary reliability. This study presents an evidence-grounded framework for evaluating LLM-assisted Android forensic reports at the atomic-claim level. Gemini, Llama, and Qwen each generated reports for two controlled cases: a public Android 13 dataset and a physical LG device with a zero-reportable-fact boundary. articles.title: ValiAssist: Scaling LLM-generated Programming Feedback Validation by Demonstration
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI can create programming feedback at scale, but validating its alignment with instructors' pedagogical goals and strategies remains challenging. Instructors may struggle to fully specify validation criteria upfront, as these often emerge through inspecting concrete examples and revising misaligned feedback. articles.title: AI and The Enclosure of the Scientific Commons
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The scientific literature can be viewed as an "information commons:" an intangible resource that "no one owns and is shared by everyone." There are well-established economic and political frameworks for understanding such commons, emerging from the history of agricultural common lands found in places like preindustrial England. articles.title: Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence is widely assumed to scale with effort: more researchers, papers and investment should accelerate discovery. Theories of technological growth instead locate the difficulty of discovery in the space of ideas. Here we show that neither scale nor space is enough: breakthroughs depend on diverse attention, which collective concentration can deplete. articles.title: District Size Matters: How Seats Per District Shapes Proportionality Under STV
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the impact of utilizing multimember districts and Single Transferable Vote (STV) as the winner selection method on partisan proportionality. We start with detailed case studies of the upper legislative houses of Illinois, New Hampshire, and New Mexico, building ensembles of redistricting maps with mostly 2-member, mostly 3-member, and mostly 4-member districts for each state. articles.title: Choose your own adventure: How data source selection shapes urban accessibility analyses
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.27390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Urban park accessibility shapes mental health, physical well-being, and community cohesion. Measuring it is thus central to urban and landscape planning. Although researchers have debated the impacts of different accessibility measures on analysis results, scant attention has been paid to variability from data source selection. Do the results of accessibility analyses vary depending on the dataset used to define park locations and attributes?
